title: Multi-analyte Biochip (MAB) Based on All-solid-state Ion-selective Electrodes (ASSISE) for Physiological Research
protocol: Add 70 mg poly(sodium 4-styrenesulfonate) (Na+PSS-) to 10 ml deionized (DI) water and vortex until completely dispersed.
Add 10.7 μl 3,4-ethlyenedioxythiophene (EDOT) to the solution in step above and vortex until solution is completely mixed.
Add 136 mg calcium sulphate (CaSO4) to 10 ml DI water and vortex; the solution will not completely disperse and appears milky.
Add 10.7 μl EDOT to the CaSO4 solution in previous step and vortex until completely mixed.
Place the EDOT:PSS electropolymerization solution in the electrochemical cell and nitrogen bubble for 20 min to remove dissolved oxygen.
Clip a platinum-gauze at the counter electrode position of the electrochemical cell.
Clip the MAB at the working electrode position with the working electrodes facing the platinum-gauze.
Adjust the MAB depth so that only the circular electrodes are submerged in the PEDOT:PSS electropolymerization solution.
Avoid solution contact with the square electrical contact pads.
Place a BASI saturated silver/silver chloride (Ag/AgCl) electrode in the reference electrode position of the electrochemical cell.
Ensure the reference electrode is not positioned between the working and counter electrodes.
Bubble the electrochemical cell for 20 minutes.
Use the EC epsilon potentiostat/galvanostat to run a single cyclic voltammogram from 0V - 1.1V with a scan rate of 20 mV/sec on a ±100 μA scale.
Bubble the electrochemical cell for 20 minutes.
Use the EC epsilon potentiostat/galvanostat to run chronopotentiometry at 814 nA for 30 minutes.
Perform steps 3.1-3.3 above as specified.
Run single cyclic voltammograms from -653 mV to 853 mV with varying scan rates of (25, 50, 75, 100, l25, 150, 175, 200) mV/sec on a ±10 μA scale.
Deposit conductive polymer conjugate specific for the ions of interest as in Step 3.
Apply ion-selective membrane as in Step 6.
Center the MAB on the vacuum spinner chuck.
Deposit 100 μl membrane onto the center of the MAB.
Spin-coat ion-selective membrane with a spin coater at 1,500 rpm for 30 sec with a 5 sec ramp up and down.
Vacuum the spin-coated MAB for 30 min.
Bake the chip in an oven at 70 °C for 20 min.
Condition the MAB overnight in 10 μM sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) and 5 mM potassium chloride (KCl) in algal media.
Insert the MAB into the microfluidic flow-cell chip holder.
Inject 5 ml test solution with initial pH value or concentration (e.g., pH 4 or 10 μM for CO32-).
Remove bubbles from the flow-cell chip holder.
Place the flow-cell chip holder onto the flow-cell electrical fixture.
Open the EC epsilon software and enter open-circuit potential (OP) mode.
Set the time to 300 min, the voltage scale to ± 1V, and the cutoff frequency to 10 kHz.
Record the value every 2 sec.
Let the MAB stabilize before continuing with the calibration process.
Flush the flow cell with test solution when stabilized.
Inject the next concentration to be calibrated (pH 5 or 25 μM CO32-).
Ensure no bubbles enter the flow cell during injection.
Repeat steps for pH 6, 7, 8, and 9 or CO32- concentrations of 50, 75, 100, 250, 500, 750, and 1,000 μM.
Remove the MAB after the last concentration has run.
Dry the MAB with nitrogen air.
Place the MAB back into fresh conditioning solution until next use.
Condition the MAB overnight in 7 ml of 0.1 M CaCl2 and 10 μM NaNO3.
Follow steps similar to 7.2 - 7.10 for calibration.
Replace carbonate test solution with an initial concentration of 0.01 mM CaCl2.
Repeat for test-solution concentrations of 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1 and 10 mM.
